articles.title: Why 27,854 route pages need a different sitemap strategy
articles.excerpt: When a site grows to 27,854 route pages, the sitemap stops being a formality and becomes a strategy decision. Search engines will not crawl everything equally, so the question is not how to list every…
articles.body: When a site grows to 27,854 route pages, the sitemap stops being a formality and becomes a strategy decision. Search engines will not crawl everything equally, so the question is not how to list every page, it is how to tell crawlers which pages matter, which pages are new, and which pages can wait. The first mistake we made was one giant sitemap. It was technically valid and practically useless: it hid the important pages among thousands of near-identical route pages, and when something changed, the whole file had to be regenerated. We split it into smaller sitemaps by route type and by region, so a change to one group only touches that group's file, and the sitemap index tells crawlers exactly where to look. The second mistake was treating all routes as equal.

The 14 impressions it did report cannot be tied to any query. Crawling, speed and schema were all fine. Google's URL Inspection tool lists exactly one outside page linking to us, a post we published ourselves. That is the whole diagnosis. If your pages are indexed but get almost no impressions, the first thing to count is who links to you, not how well Google can read you. Below is the evidence, the API behind each number, and what we do not know. We make Lullwood, so this is our own site's data. articles.body: 裝潢有完工清單，政府採購有驗收標準，但 GEO 這一行的交付長期是模糊的。 模糊對買方不利：你說不出少了什麼，就沒辦法要求補齊。這篇把四塊工作、七項交付物寫成可以直接勾選的清單。 今天就用一篇文章給你講清楚， GEO 優化能給到你什麼。 第一塊：先給你搭一份企業知識庫 這是整套 GEO 的地基，也是我們開工做的第一件事。 說白了，就是把你散在各處的企業事實，收攏成一份結構化的、說法統一的知識底座。它不是一份介紹公司的簡報，是一個倉庫—— 所有能被 AI 用來認識你的事實，都裝在裡面。 ［2］［3］ 為什麼這塊排第一？ 你想，你的資訊現在散在哪兒：老闆腦子裡、業務的嘴上、幾張產品型錄裡，還有幾篇早就過時的舊新聞。這些地方的東西，AI 一個都讀不到。它讀得到的，只有你放到網路上的、而且結構化了的那些。 所以第一件事，是先把這些事實聚起來、理清楚。 這個倉庫裡，裝六類東西： 你是誰 ：品牌名、公司全名、登記地、官網網域，一套說清楚，不許有第二種寫法 你做什麼 ：產品、服務、規格參數，具體到能被驗證——不是「效能優異」，是「重複定位精度 ±0.003 mm」這樣的數字 你服務誰 ：客戶是誰、典型場景是什麼，別寫「為各行業提供解決方案」 你憑什麼 ：證照、案例、第三方報導，一條一條掛上來源 你的邊界 ：你不接什麼、做不到什麼。這條最容易被省，但 AI 很看重——敢說邊界的，反而更像真的 你的原話 ：權威、可驗證的第三方評價，能拿來對外引用的原話 它分兩層，你得知道區別： 一層是 事實層 ，帶來源、帶邊界，給人和業務用——寫稿前查事實、業務應答、合規核對，都從這裡找。 另一層是 答案層 ，把事實層裡那些「給 AI 看」的部分單獨剝出來，一題一份標準答案，措辭乾淨、不帶內部標註，專門拿去餵 AI、統一對外說法。 怎麼驗收？給你一把能當場用的量尺： 隨便從你客戶嘴裡挑一個問題，5 分鐘之內…

articles.title: Going Deeper With Memories: Deep Dive & Engineering Breakdown
articles.excerpt: Going Deeper With Memories: Architecting Byte-Level LLMs with DeepMem For years, the Large Language Model stack has been anchored by a noisy abstraction: the tokenizer. Whether you rely on Byte-Pair E…
articles.body: Going Deeper With Memories: Architecting Byte-Level LLMs with DeepMem For years, the Large Language Model stack has been anchored by a noisy abstraction: the tokenizer. Whether you rely on Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE), WordPiece, or Unigram models, tokenizers introduce structural vulnerabilities. They suffer from out-of-vocabulary (OOV) failures, bloat sequence lengths on non-English text, struggle with mathematical notation and source code, and add an unneeded pre-processing bottleneck. Byte-level language models eliminate this friction entirely. By ingesting raw UTF-8 bytes directly, they provide universal coverage and structural purity. There is just one engineering wall: Quadratic compute cost. Processing raw byte streams at full resolution explodes sequence lengths.

articles.title: Designing search for 56,000 games: what actually helps players find a game
articles.excerpt: Running a portal with 56,000 browser games sounds like a search problem, and it is, but not the kind most search advice covers. Players do not arrive with a precise query. They arrive with a mood, ten…
articles.body: Running a portal with 56,000 browser games sounds like a search problem, and it is, but not the kind most search advice covers. Players do not arrive with a precise query. They arrive with a mood, ten free minutes, and a vague idea like something relaxing or something with cars. Search that only matches exact titles fails them, because they do not know the titles yet. The first lesson was that categories matter more than keywords. A player who clicks puzzle games is not searching, they are browsing with intent, and the category page is the search result. We rebuilt category pages to load instantly, show the most played games first, and keep the filters visible, so a player can narrow from puzzle to word puzzle to crossword in two clicks without typing anything.

articles.title: A Supabase row-level security checklist for multi-role apps (from a 163-policy production schema)
articles.excerpt: I run a production app on Supabase with eight user roles: field reps, team leads, business leads, key account managers, admins, directors, accounts and logistics. Each sees a different slice of the sa…
articles.body: I run a production app on Supabase with eight user roles: field reps, team leads, business leads, key account managers, admins, directors, accounts and logistics. Each sees a different slice of the same tables. The schema has 64 tables and 163 row-level security policies, and the client is never trusted with any of it. This is the checklist I now apply to every table and function. It's ordered by how badly things break if you skip it. 1. RLS on every table. No exceptions, no "internal" tables alter table public . vehicle_inspections enable row level security ; A table without RLS is readable by any signed-in user through the auto-generated API. "Nobody queries that table from the app" doesn't matter, because anybody can call the API directly.

The remake, which is releasing 28 years after the launch of the original version on Nintendo 64, has a much more realistic visual style and some modern improvements like a jump button, a way to sprint, full voice acting, and a “Threads of Time” feature that helps you keep track of your progress. But while the game has a new coat of paint, it appears many elements will still remain faithful to the classic N64 release. articles.title: NASA asks industry for ideas about saving Hubble Space Telescope
articles.excerpt: The Hubble Space Telescope is healthy but is being pulled down toward Earth by atmospheric drag. NASA is considering options to extend the iconic telescope's work.
articles.body: NASA is reviving discussions to rescue the Hubble Space Telescope, which is operating well but is on track to reenter Earth's atmosphere about six years from now. The agency issued a request for information (RFI) on Oct. 29 for "in-space servicing" capabilities, which could include boosting Hubble's orbit (which is naturally degrading due to atmospheric drag), or even a mission to "enhance its capabilities" in some way. Hubble, which launched in April 1990 in partnership with the European Space Agency , was serviced five times by astronauts on space shuttle missions, the most recent being in 2009.

articles.title: Ancient star collisions could explain mysterious Little Red Dots and 'impossible' black holes
articles.excerpt: Collisions between stars in the early universe were common, and this could explain the growth of supermassive black holes and the existence of strange Little Red Dots seen by the James Webb Space Tele…
articles.body: New research suggests that collisions between stars in the early universe were common, which could help explain the rapid growth of supermassive black holes and the existence of strange Little Red Dots seen by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). The team behind this research performed simulations of the early universe and found stellar systems were densely packed, leading to stars frequently slamming into each other. While rapid collisions would have destroyed the stars involved, slower collisions would have led to repeated mergers, creating single over-massive stars, which could collapse and form larger-than-usual black holes at the end of their lives. These could be the seeds of the first supermassive black holes.

articles.body: The three Americans currently living off Earth just made sure their electoral voices were heard. Anil Menon told us today (Nov. 3) that he and fellow NASA astronauts Luke Delaney and Jessica Watkins voted in the U.S. midterm elections from the International Space Station (ISS). "Yes, you can even vote from space! All three U.S. crew members had the privilege of voting from space station.
